commands.author: hugenshen

target.title: fix(mattermost): truncate inbound preview on code-point boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Mattermost inbound handler in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts` builds a verbose log preview with `bodyText.slice(0, 200)`. When an emoji or other astral character straddles the 200 UTF-16 code-unit boundary, that raw slice can emit a **lone surrogate** into the preview string. Downstream consumers that expect well-formed UTF-16 can reject or mis-render the preview.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the raw `.slice(0, 200)` with the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, matching the surrogate-safe preview pattern already used by Slack, Discord, Telegram, IRC, Line, MS Teams, and Feishu channel previews.

## User Impact

Cosmetic logging only: when the 200th code unit would split an emoji, the verbose inbound preview now omits the partial emoji instead of logging a broken surrogate. No message delivery or routing behavior changes.

## Evidence

```bash
node --import tsx scripts/proof-mattermost-inbound-preview-bound.mjs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-inbound-preview.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Mattermost verbose inbound log previews must not contain lone UTF-16 surrogates when truncation lands inside an emoji surrogate pair.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin), Node.js v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node --import tsx scripts/proof-mattermost-inbound-preview-bound.mjs`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-inbound-preview.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-mattermost-inbound-preview-bound.mjs
  ok: raw slice(0, 200) leaves a lone surrogate at emoji boundary
  ok: truncateUtf16Safe preview has no lone surrogates
  ok: preview drops the split emoji instead of emitting \uD83D
preview length=199

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-inbound-preview.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ does not split a surrogate pair at the 200-unit preview cap
 ✓ escapes newlines after surrogate-safe truncation

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** For a body with 199 `a` characters followed by 😀, raw `slice(0, 200)` contains a lone high surrogate; the Mattermost preview helper path using `truncateUtf16Safe` returns 199 well-formed `a` characters with no surrogate halves.
- **What was not tested:** Live Mattermost websocket ingest against a real server; proof exercises the production `truncateUtf16Safe` import used by `monitor.ts`.

## Tests and validation

- `node --import tsx scripts/proof-mattermost-inbound-preview-bound.mjs`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-inbound-preview.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- Regression tests in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-inbound-preview.test.ts`

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Yes — verbose log preview may omit a trailing emoji when truncation would have split its surrogate pair.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? No
- Highest-risk area: verbose logging only
- Mitigation: matches sibling channel preview truncation behavior; message handling unchanged

## AI-assisted disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
- [x] Human-run Real behavior proof from local setup
